source.title: Loss Barcode: A Topological Measure of Escapability in Loss Landscapes
source.authors: S. Barannikov; D. Voronkova; A. Mironenko; I. Trofimov; Alexander Korotin; Grigorii Sotnikov; Evgeny Burnaev

record.tranche_reason: Measures whether loss-barcode properties track generalization across trained minima, using a different measure from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Section 5 reports test accuracy and loss for minima with nearly equal training loss, and states that barcode segments differ with generalization. The paper does not test the listed versions’ specific interventions or measurements; its other architecture and optimization results concern barcode geometry, not those versions’ outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study measures loss-barcode topology and its association with held-out performance, which does not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure. Its width comparisons also do not establish V2's required widening beyond zero training error. No other version's specified comparison is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase accurately summarizes Section 5: lower barcode barriers accompany better generalization in the examined comparisons. The authors also conclude that barcodes characterize optimization obstacles and landscape complexity. Their generalization finding is an observed association in certain situations, not a validated universal ranking rule.
record.recipe_differences: Studies loss-barcode geometry and its association with generalization; it does not test the listed interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported association differs between constant-small-learning-rate and annealed-learning-rate minima, on both CIFAR10 and SVHN.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR10 and SVHN, annealed-learning-rate ResNet-like models have higher test accuracy and lower barcode saddle losses than constant-small-learning-rate models with similarly low training loss. Training budgets also differ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss-barcode escape barriers distinguish generalization performance between these training procedures; the association is correlational.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 8 reports that widening ResNet-56 raises test accuracy from 93.96667% to 95.00000%, and widening its counterpart without skip connections raises accuracy from 89.08667% to 91.99667%. Narrower-model training accuracies are 99.99067% and 99.54000%, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Widening these convolutional networks improves held-out accuracy, without establishing improvement beyond an exact zero-training-error threshold.

record.problems: Section 5 compares only two learning-rate procedures and reports an association, not a causal test. The paper says the minima have similar, nearly zero training loss; it does not report random-label fitting or evaluate the specific measures and interventions in the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional Section 5 result rows omitted. Other reported architecture, batch-normalization, transformer, and polynomial findings concern barcode values or optimization behavior without measuring a listed version’s specified outcome.

untested.parts: No random-label training or matched natural-label versus random-label generalization comparison.

No width comparison establishing that the narrower network already reaches zero training error. Section 6 reports widening benefits in convolutional networks, but does not establish the claimed post-interpolation condition.
No matched convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison or test of learned local connectivity.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison of held-out performance.
No batch-size comparison of held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout intervention or comparison removing dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness measurement or comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings. Global escape barriers measure a different property.
No removal of memorized examples or comparison with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T2 classification conflicts with its correct observation that none of V1–V8 is measured. Section 6 does report held-out architecture comparisons, contrary to the record's blanket characterization of those results as geometry-only; they still do not establish V2's post-interpolation premise. States marked cannot_determine refer to the listed versions, not uncertainty that the reported accuracy differences exist.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on random labels or compare natural-label and random-label test performance.
Does not test one-hidden-layer ReLU width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Does not compare convolutional networks with fully connected networks for image generalization as specified.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD for held-out performance.
Does not vary batch size or test large-batch generalization penalties.
Does not test dropout or its removal.
Does not measure magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness or compare its ranking with norm- or margin-based measures.
Does not remove memorized training examples or compare their effect with random removals.

rows.subject: ResNet-like models (195k trainable parameters)
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy for minima trained with a small constant learning rate (type 1) and annealing (type 2); authors report lower barcode saddle-point losses for type 2.
rows.locator: Section 5; Figure 6; Table 7 in Appendix H
rows.note: Compared minima have nearly zero and similar training loss; Table 7 reports type 1 test accuracy as 72.66125 ± 0.82658%.
rows.check: The accuracy comparison measures no listed version. Section 5 and Figure 6 give the baseline as 80.64 ± 0.41%, whereas Table 7 gives 80.83000 ± 0.25070%; this discrepancy should be explicit. Table 1 also shows different training budgets: 4500 epochs for type 1 versus 300 for type 2.
